 A Missouri law says utilities cannot disconnect any heat-related service when temperatures fall below freezing for an extended period.

 Missouri's cold weather law kicks in Saturday, meaning local utilities cannot disconnect any heat-related service when temperatures fall below freezing for an extended period.
 The law, passed in 2025, stipulates that heat must remain in service when temperatures are predicted to drop below 32 degrees between 6 a.m. and 9  p.m. for a 72-hour period. The law remains in effect until March 31. 
 The law was updated last year to extend the forecast protection period from 24 hours to 72 hours. Added consumer protections for eligible customers include more lenient payment terms, extended payment plans and notification requirements prior to disconnection, according to the Missouri Public Service Commission.
 Customers who are disabled or over age 65 may register with their utility to receive additional assistance.
 An established procedure needs to be followed when utility bills cannot be paid. Steps include contacting the utility company, explaining why the bill cannot be paid in full, providing documentation, making a minimum payment if required and possibly setting up a payment agreement.
 For more information on the Cold Weather Law, consumers can visit the Missouri Public Service Commission’s website at www.psc.mo.gov or call the Commission’s Consumer Services hotline at 1-800-392-4211.
 Local utilities can also give customers more information.
